messages:
alex: FYI postmortem follow-up from last night's latency spike. I drafted proposed SLO/SLA updates and action items below. Please read and ack if you own anything.

maya: reading. quick summary?

jordan: high level: p95 drifted to ~420ms for ~18m, p99 ~1.2s. error rate stayed low but request queuing increased on gateway during a small autoscale gap.

alex: +1. root cause: mis-tuned autoscale cooldown + a rollout that temporarily reduced available workers. kubernetes HPA didn't react fast enough for the sudden seq len increase.

samir: we saw recurring pattern in the last two months where seq-length spikes coincide with afternoon batch jobs. might need a protective SLO guard or rate-limit.

alex: proposed SLO/SLA updates:
- keep availability SLA at 99.95% (no change for customers)
- internal latency SLOs (serving path): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 800ms (these will be used for error budget calculations)
- throughput SLO: sustained 1000 RPS for hosted tier-1 with burst to 2000 RPS (useful for load tests)
- introduce an "autoscale safety" SLO: 99.9% of scale events must complete within 90s when needed (detects scaling gaps)

maya: curious what baseline numbers are today vs these proposed.

jordan: current baseline (30d): p95 180ms, p99 600ms, sustained RPS ~1200 average, but with occasional 10–20m windows where p95 jumps to 400ms. so proposed p95 is a little looser than current median but gives headroom for complex workloads.

alex: action items (owners + due dates):
- A1: update SLO docs and error-budget computation to include new latency SLOs and autoscale safety metric — owner: @maya — due: 2024-05-10
- A2: dashboard + alerting: add Grafana panel for autoscale event duration and an alert when autoscale fails >30s for >3 events/hr — owner: @jordan — due: 2024-04-28
- A3: runbook: add mitigation steps for autoscale gap including manual scale commands and quick rollback playbook — owner: @samir — due: 2024-04-25
- A4: infra: enforce canary rollout guard to keep at least 20% capacity untouched during deploys for 48h after config changes — owner: @eng-release (tracked by release lead) — due: 2024-05-02
- A5: product ops: communicate customer-facing SLA recertification and include a note about no change to availability SLA — owner: @product-ops — due: 2024-05-05

samir: I'll pair with infra tomorrow to add the manual scale commands to runbook.

jordan: for dashboards I suggest adding an error-budget burn rate view that ties latency SLO violations to specific deployments and autoscale events. will add a Grafana alert + Datadog synthetic check.

maya: ack A1. I'll also update the internal SLO page and add an example of how we compute consumed error budget per incident.

incident-bot: Incident #2024-117 logged: autoscale gap / latency spike. Severity: S2. Postmortem assigned to alex.

alex: two process asks: 1) can we make SLO changes internal-only for 30 days before public doc change? want to monitor burn after change. 2) let's add a recurring 2-week check-in for 8 weeks to watch for recurrence.

product-ops: we can do internal-only SLO window. we'll hold public SLA doc until after 30d review.

jordan: timeline for dashboards looks like 2 working days for initial panels, then iterate. I'll post PR for alert rules.

samir: adding runbook edits today, will post snippet:
```
# Manual scale helper
kubectl scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=10 -n prod
# fallback to previous deployment
kubectl rollout undo deployment inference-gateway -n prod
```

alex: good. follow-up cadence: we'll reconvene in #eng-sre thread in one week. please update the action item owners in the PRs so we can mark them closed.

maya: created SLO doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-docs/pull/184 — includes new SLO numbers and error budget formula.

jordan: created grafana dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abc123/serving-slo-overview — sharing in the channel.

alex: thanks team. last ask: if anyone sees related latency spikes in next 30d, ping me + tag incident-bot so we can link to this postmortem for trend analysis. :thumbsup:

product-ops: noted. will coordinate any customer comms after the 30d review.

maya: ack, closing my action item once PR lands and CI passes.

alex: last_message: documented in our follow-up tracker. repeating owners: A1@maya, A2@jordan, A3@samir, A4@eng-release, A5@product-ops.
